title: Protocol for measuring protein synthesis in specific cell types in the mouse brain using in vivo non-canonical amino acid tagging
protocol: Put mice on a methionine-deficient diet for seven days.
Dissolve 5 mg of AHA in 500 μL sterile 0.9% saline solution to achieve a concentration of 10 μg/μL.
Vortex the vial containing dissolved AHA.
Inject AHA intraperitoneally at a dose of 100 μg per gram of body weight.
Return mice to their home cages after AHA injection.
Dissolve anisomycin in sterile saline solution to obtain a concentration of 40 μM.
Inject anisomycin intraperitoneally at a dose of 100 mg/kg one hour before AHA injection for control group.
Minimize stress levels by returning mice to their home cages immediately after injections.
Keep the cage in a quiet and well-ventilated place until perfusion step.
Anesthetize the mouse using an anesthesia machine.
Place the mouse in an anesthesia induction chamber where it inhales oxygen mixed with 3%–5% isoflurane.
Transfer the unconscious mouse to a nose cone connected to the anesthesia machine for stable anesthesia maintenance.
Adjust the oxygen flowmeter to 0.4–0.8 L/min and set the isoflurane to 2%–2.5%.
Assess the anesthesia level by pinching the tail or toe with tweezers.
Start perfusion only if the surgical level of anesthesia is met.
Perfuse the mouse transcardially with 10 mL of 1× PBS using a peristaltic pump at 30 RPM (∼2 mL/5 s).
Switch to 4% PFA and continue perfusing with 50–100 mL of PFA based on tail and limb stiffness.
Place the anesthetized mouse on its back, tape the four paws to a perfusion board.
Expose the heart through surgical incisions.
Insert a 28-gauge needle into the left ventricle apex for perfusion.
Expose the skull by cutting and peeling skin and muscles from the head.
Hold the skull firmly with forceps while cutting through it to expose the brain.
Gently scoop out the brain after detaching cranial nerves and blood vessels.
Post-fix the extracted brain in 7–10 mL of 4% PFA for 12–18 hours at 20°C–22°C.
Prepare ice-cold 1× PBS by placing it at −20°C for 20–30 minutes before use.
Locate the cerebellum on the brain dorsal side and make a transverse cut rostral to the cerebellum, discarding the caudal part.
Fill the slicing chamber of the vibratome with ice-cold 1× PBS and add ice to the tray surrounding the chamber.
Mount a razor blade on the blade holder of the vibratome.
Set the vibratome cutting thickness at 40 μm.
Set the vibratome speed to 0.36 mm/s and amplitude to 1.20 mm.
Mount the brain onto the cutting stage of the vibratome using super glue, with the rostral side up and dorsal side facing the blade.
Start cutting by slowly lowering the cutting blade into the 1× PBS solution until it touches the brain’s surface.
Collect coronal sections in a 24-well plate filled with 1× PBS.
Transfer free-floating sections to wells pre-filled with 1 mL of 1× PBS using a paint brush.
Select three sections per cortical area/animal and transfer them to a new 24-well plate.
Wash cortical sections 6 times for 5 min each with 500 μL PBS on rocking shaker at 50 RPM at the 20°C–22°C.
Block the sections for 12–18 h at 4°C in 500 μL of blocking buffer containing 0.05% Triton X-100, 10% normal goat serum, and 5% sucrose in PBS on orbital shaker with gentle agitation at 20 RPM.
Perform 6 washes of 5 min using PBS on rocking shaker with gentle agitation (20–30 RPM).
Incubate the sections in 500 μL of click buffer for 12–18 h at 4°C and keep the plate on a shaker at 20 RPM speed.
Prepare fresh PBS at 20°C–22°C.
Add 1 μL of 200 mM TRIzol per 1 mL of click buffer.
Vortex the buffer with high speed for 10 s.
Add 1 μL of 500 mM TCEP per 1 mL of click buffer.
Vortex the buffer with high speed for 10 s.
Add 1 μL of 2 mM fluorescent Alexa Fluor 647 alkyne per 1 mL of click buffer.
Vortex the buffer with high speed for 10 s.
Add 1 μL of 200 mM CuSO4 per 1 mL of click buffer.
Vortex the buffer with high speed for 30 s.
Label different neuronal types using primary antibodies against CaMKIIα and GAD67.
Wash the sections 10 times for 5 min each with 500 μL of "FUNCAT wash buffer" consisting of 0.5 mM EDTA and 1% Tween-20 in PBS on a rocking shaker at 50 RPM.
Transfer the sections to a new 24-well plate.
Block the sections with 500 μL of IHC blocking buffer (1% normal goat serum in PBS) for 1 hour at 20°C–22°C on an orbital shaker at 20 RPM.
Incubate the blocked sections in 500 μL of primary antibody of interest for 12–18 hours at 4°C on an orbital shaker.
Wash the sections 3 times for 5 min each with 500 μL PBS on a rocking shaker.
Incubate the sections in 500 μL of corresponding secondary antibody (such as Alexa Fluor 488, 1:500 dilution) at 20°C–22°C on orbital shaker for 1 h.
Wash the sections 3 times for 5 min each at 20°C–22°C with 500 μL of PBS.
Prepare the glass slides, coverslips, and mounting media.
Mount the sections on the slides and cover each section with 20 μL of DAPI-containing mounting media.
Place the coverslips, apply the sealant (nail polish), and allow the slides to dry at 20°C–22°C for 2 h.
Keep the slides at 4°C in darkness.
Image the slides using a confocal microscope.
Use the 63× oil objective in Z-stack mode to capture images.
Ensure the objective lens is clean and properly aligned.
Place one slide on the microscope stage, adjust the stage and the pinhole size for confocal microscopy.
Choose lasers with appropriate wavelengths of interest and select proper emission and excitation filters to allow specific wavelengths to pass through.
Adjust laser power to an optimal level.
Choose Z-stacks mode and start imaging.
Take 15–20 optical sections spaced at 2–2.5 μm intervals from each region of interest.
Image at least 3 sections per area for each mouse.
Merge all Z-stacks using Image >> Stacks >> Z project >> Max intensity on ImageJ.
Open the merged image using ImageJ.
Select the marker channel, such as the CAMKIIα channel (red).
Using the marker, select one neuron.
Make a region of interest (ROI) that fits inside the cytoplasm of the neuron.
Measure the integrated density of the AHA signal in the cytoplasm.
Select the DAPI channel alongside the AHA channel.
Only if there is no overlap, de-select the DAI channel.
Relocate the ROI if it overlaps with the nucleus.
Select the AHA channel before measuring the integrated density of the AHA.
Maintain consistent dimensions of the ROI across all images and experimental groups.
Save the ROI dimensions using Ctrl + T key command.
Quantify the AHA signal in 20–40 excitatory neurons or 10 to 20 inhibitory neurons.
Normalize and analyze the data.
Divide all values for the control and Fmr1-/y groups by the control’s average.
Multiply the result by 100 to normalize the data.
Restrict quantification to the cytoplasm.
Average the values from each mouse.
